s: The stateless application server hosting core business logic, validating inputs, orchestrating calls to data stores and downstream services.
w: Receives requests from gateways or load balancers, executes domain logic (validation, authorization, transformation), queries databases/caches, and returns structured responses. Typically deployed as horizontally scalable containers behind a load balancer. Each instance is stateless; all persistent state lives in databases or caches. Health checks route traffic only to healthy instances.
use: Core CRUD and business logic for any product domain
Request validation, transformation, and orchestration of downstream calls
Enforcing business rules that span multiple data sources
Serving as the authoritative backend for web and mobile clients
avoid: Heavy background processing (use worker nodes instead to avoid request latency)
Stateful long-lived connections like websockets (use websocket_gateway)
Direct database writes without business logic (wasted hop)

props.timeout_ms: Per-request deadline before the caller gets a 504
props.replicas: Horizontal instance count behind the load balancer

pat.d: API reads from replicas/cache, writes to primary - simple read/write split.
New API handles fresh routes while legacy handles old - gateway routes between them.

pits: Chatty downstream calls multiply latency - batch or use DataLoader/gRPC multiplexing
Missing timeouts cascade - set connect/read/write timeouts on every outbound call
N+1 database queries from ORM eager-loading misconfig - profile query counts per request
tips: Emphasize stateless design enabling horizontal scaling - any instance can handle any request
Discuss timeout budgets: if gateway is 5s and DB is 2s, API call budget is <3s with headroom
Mention the distinction between API (request/response) and worker (background) compute
